statements.status_notes: Upstream fixed this ECDH buffer overwrite (GnuPG T8211, https://dev.gnupg.org/T8211) in Libgcrypt 1.12.2, 1.11.3 and 1.10.4; see the release announcement https://lists.gnupg.org/pipermail/gnupg-announce/2026q2/000503.html. The fix is upstream commit 2d3d732c9bf87cc10729f69678dd9e6862f99fa3 (cipher/ecc-misc.c, _gcry_ecc_mont_decodepoint), which is in the 1.12.2, 1.12.3 and 1.12.4 releases and not in 1.11.2. This package is built from the unmodified upstream release tarball. The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository publishes libgcrypt 1.11.2-r0, 1.12.2-r0, 1.12.3-r0 and 1.12.4-r0 for x86_64 and aarch64; the shared library in each identifies itself as the matching upstream release (its version banner, for example Libgcrypt 1.12.2 in the 1.12.2-r0 build). 1.11.2-r0 lacks the fix and is affected; 1.12.2-r0 and later carry it. Upgrade to 1.12.2-r0 or later.

CVE-2026-41989: libgcrypt before 1.12.2 can overflow a heap buffer when gcry_pk_decrypt decodes a crafted ECDH ciphertext point on a Montgomery curve, because _gcry_ecc_mont_decodepoint() pads short input incorrectly (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-41989, https://dev.gnupg.org/T8211, https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/04/21/1). Upstream fixed it in libgcrypt commit 2d3d732c9bf87cc10729f69678dd9e6862f99fa3 (libgcrypt 1.12.2); the bug was introduced in 1.9.0. Debian backported that commit to trixie in 1.11.0-7+deb13u1 (DSA-6294-1). The DHI libgcrypt20 package for Debian 13 is a rebuild of Debian's 1.11.0-7+deb13u1; the one build the DHI Debian repository publishes (amd64 and arm64), which is the fixed version used here, ships a Debian changelog that records the Montgomery-curve point decoding fix for CVE-2026-41989.
